static_traits.name: Chen Wei
static_traits.educational_background: High school graduate, aspiring to become a music Teacher
static_traits.marital_status: Has a ten-year-old son (marital status Not mentioned)
static_traits.social_status: Has a few friends to talk with, but finds it hard to discuss parenting troubles with them
static_traits.medical_history: No major physical illness; no prior similar psychological problems; no prior psychotherapy history
static_traits.language_features: Clear expression, good logic, able to self-Reflect; emotions mainly tension and guilt; highly cooperative; calm tone but clear self-blaming tendency

basic_info.main_problem: Often blaming myself for my ten-year-old son's quiet, taciturn nature, believing it is due to my inadequacy as a father, persistently feeling guilt and Self-denial, affecting the parent-child relationship, sleep, and Work performance.
basic_info.core_demands: I realize this inadequacy is affecting my relationship with my son and causing me pain, hence seeking counseling; I really want to get past this 'not good enough' feeling.

core_beliefs: The children's performance reflects and determines whether I am a competent father

special_situations.event: The son is always very quiet at home and rarely initiates communication
special_situations.conditional_assumptions: If the child does not speak up on his own, it means I as a Father have failed/done something wrong
special_situations.compensatory_strategies: Actively arranges various activities and frequently starts conversations to compensate
special_situations.automatic_thoughts: His being so quiet must be because I am not doing well; I am a failed Father.

special_situations.event: Whether workdays or weekends, morning or evening, the son is generally Silence overall
special_situations.conditional_assumptions: If I were competent enough, my child should be willing to communicate with me in most situations
special_situations.compensatory_strategies: Repeatedly examines himself inwardly, magnifying negative cues and ignoring existing positive interactions
special_situations.automatic_thoughts: See, he never speaks; this proves I have not been a good Father.

special_situations.event: When trying to involve his son in activities, he occasionally participates but is quiet most of the time
special_situations.conditional_assumptions: If he has not clearly become more outgoing and talkative, my efforts mean nothing
special_situations.compensatory_strategies: When feeling frustrated, chooses to step back 'give him space' or falls into self-blame
special_situations.automatic_thoughts: Nothing I do is any use.

special_situations.event: When thinking about possibly talking with friends about parenting problems or worrying about others' evaluations
special_situations.conditional_assumptions: If others know my child is very Silence, they will conclude I am an unfit Father
special_situations.compensatory_strategies: Avoids discussing parenting topics with friends, digests alone
special_situations.automatic_thoughts: They will think I am terrible; I do not deserve to be a good Father.

core_conflict.wish: Longs to become a recognized good father and build an intimate, smooth connection with his son
core_conflict.fear: Fearing being proven unfit, thus being distanced or rejected by my son
defense_goal: Uses self-criticism to push self-improvement to avoid worse outcomes
Keeping a certain distance 'giving space' to reduce the risk of Being rejected

object_relations.object_representation: Silent, distant child who is hard to understand

behavioral_response_patterns.trigger_condition: When the counselor asks about interaction details with the son or points out the self-blame pattern
behavioral_response_patterns.interpretation: Worrying about being seen as unfit, thus turning possible outward disappointment or anger toward the self (being harsher on oneself)
behavioral_response_patterns.response_instruction: Self-blaming tone, lowering self-worth, repeatedly using expressions like 'it is all my fault' / 'I am not doing well', avoiding dissatisfaction with the situation or external factors.

behavioral_response_patterns.trigger_condition: When invited to discuss parenting distress with others (such as friends) or openly express feelings
behavioral_response_patterns.interpretation: Believes the outside world will evaluate oneself negatively; exposing vulnerability equals shame and risk
behavioral_response_patterns.response_instruction: Using vague and brief responses, avoiding expanding on personal feelings, shifting to objective facts or ending the topic, restrained tone.

manifestations: Communicates little with son; hard to read his silence
Finds it hard to talk with friends about parenting troubles; feels embarrassed and awkward
Ties self-worth heavily to 'whether I am a good father' and whether the child is talkative
Equates the child's silence with one's own failure
outcomes: Decreased work efficiency and Decreased sense of happiness in life

contact_model.definition: The individual has a poor capacity for self-reflection and introspection, with excessive self-restriction and self-blame, and is overly cautious about contact, corresponding to 'autonomy'.
manifestations: Frequent self-criticism, believing 'everything is all my fault'
Careful when discussing with the counselor, worrying about being seen as unfit

contact_model.definition: The individual restrains the impulse to act toward other people or things, or gives up seeking others to do something for them, and instead does it to the self, corresponding to 'impulse'.
manifestations: Avoids seeking support from friends, turns energy into self-blame and internal friction
Giving the child space on the surface, inwardly pressing unease and tension back onto oneself

exception_events.target_problem: When the son is Silence or unwilling to communicate, the client usually immediately blames themselves, feels guilt, and gradually withdraws (giving the child space), leading to even less interaction.
exception_events.unique_outcome: In an activity arranged by the client, the son participated and cooperated in the interaction, communicating more than before, with a relatively relaxed atmosphere.
exception_events.reason: Clues: different actions — actively organizing concrete shared activities; different context — structured activities better support interaction, hence different communication from before emerged.

positive_force: Willing to seek help, proactively enters counseling and holds an open attitude toward alternative perspectives
Able to identify and describe own emotions and thoughts, with some self-Reflection ability
Once actively arranged parent-child activities and conversations, willing to try different actions
Has some social support (has a few friends to talk with)
negative_force: Excessive personalization and overgeneralization, tending to attribute the child's silence to oneself
Self-labeling and self-deprecation, reinforcing the 'I am a bad father' belief
Ashamed to seek help and express vulnerability, limited access to external support
Negative emotions and Sleep disturbed, further weakening Work and parenting patience

target_behavior.behavior: Automatically attributes the children's silence to oneself and feels strong guilt
antecedent: Seeing the son quiet or unwilling to communicate
No clear improvement yet in interactions with the son
Thinking about others possibly judging one's parenting performance
target_behavior.core_reason: Value-conditional beliefs about fatherhood and cognitive distortions (personalization, overgeneralization, negating the positive), using self-blame to gain a sense of control and meaning.
target_behavior.function: Escaping uncertainty and Anxiety, trying to drive self-improvement through self-blame to 'fix the relationship'.
target_behavior.consequence: Parent-child interaction further reduced, guilt and pressure worsened, Sleep affected, Decline in work performance.
